newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico warns rebels not to leave Chiapas.
newsitem.headline: Mexico warns rebels not to leave Chiapas.

text.p: The Mexican government has warned Zapatista rebels not to leave their stronghold in the southern state of Chiapas until peace accords are signed.

Amid speculation masked Zapatista leaders could attend a conference of indigenous groups in Mexico City this month, the Interior Ministry said in a statement released late on Monday that such a move would be "an act of deliberate provocation."

"Going to any place not considered under the law for other political ends, without abiding by the accords, constitutes an act of deliberate provocation, which authorities will have to respond to by applying the law," the statement said.
Zapatista leader Subcommander Marcos has said the rebels aim to attend conferences countrywide for eventual transition into the Zapatista Front for National Liberation (FZNL).
The Zapatistas have said they plan to transform their guerrilla Zapatista National Liberation Army into a non-violent political force known as the FZLN.

Their supporters in Mexico City have said they should be allowed to attend the Oct. 8-12 Indigenous Congress of some 50 Mexican Indian groups in the capital, to which the Zapatista high command has been invited. Rebel chiefs have not said whether they plan to attend.

Rebels say while the new political force would not become a political party and seek elections, it would take the Zapatista message of indian rights and democracy across Mexico and act as a political watchdog to the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).

The Interior Ministry said it has suspended arrest warrants out on rebel leaders during peace talks and guaranteed the rebels' safety during transit between their jungle bases and peace talks in several cities of Chiapas.
But it added that the army would carry out the law if the Zapatistas took any action not under the terms of the peace negotiations.
"(The army's responsibility) includes the irrevocable obligation to carry out the law in the face of actions not included in the terms of the dialogue," the statement said.
At least 145 people died during the initial Zapatista revolt, but barely a shot has been fired in anger since.
